elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor
elements.evidence: "HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may ... have the right to inspect" — the auditor is Vendor's own officer, not an independent third party
No confidentiality undertaking appears in 3.4; clause is silent

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost (subject to 5% underpayment shift)
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." — unconditional Vendor cost, at least as favourable to us as the 5% carve-out

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: Clause grants a right to "inspect the records" but contains no express prohibition on access to Company systems
"not more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" satisfies the 15-day floor

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI" with no shift-back condition

reasons: The locked target was preferred, but the redline only adds the frequency cap. Three preferred elements remain absent: an independent auditor, a confidentiality undertaking binding that auditor, and an express bar on direct access to Customer systems. The auditor is expressly Vendor's own General Manager.
The fallback is fully satisfied on its material terms: once per twelve months, 30 days' notice (exceeding the 15-day floor), and unconditional Vendor cost-bearing (better than the 10% shift-back).
The cost term benefits us as drafted (no underpayment shift at any threshold), so the absent 5%/10% carve-out is a rationale note, not a deviation.

The edit changes nothing beyond inserting the frequency cap; the surrounding words in the replacement are re-stated verbatim, so the official ratio gate is a mechanical artifact rather than substantive non-minimality. A tighter operation (inserting only ", not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and") would clear the gate.
No undefined term, contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced; the notice, business-hours and cost sentences remain effective.

To reach the preferred level, add: "by an independent third-party auditor (not a competitor of the Company) bound by written confidentiality obligations, with no direct access to the Company's systems."
